prompt: A basketball's arc follows $h = 9 - (t - 2)^2$, with $h$ in feet and $t$ in seconds. The vertex is the arc's highest point. What is the MAXIMUM height, in feet?
hint: A square like $(t - 2)^2$ is never negative — its smallest value is $0$.

hints.text: A square like $(t - 2)^2$ is never negative — its smallest value is $0$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Read the vertex form: in $h = 9 - (t - 2)^2$, the squared part is never negative, so the biggest $h$ happens when it equals $0$.
$h$ is biggest when you subtract the LEAST. When does $(t - 2)^2 = 0$?
At $t = 2$ the square is $0$, so $h = 9 - 0 = 9$ feet — the maximum.

explanation: $(t - 2)^2$ is a square, so it is always $0$ or more.
$h = 9$ minus that square, so $h$ peaks when the square is $0$.
That happens at $t = 2$: maximum height $= 9 - 0 = 9$ feet.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test times around the peak
steps: Heights rise to 9 and fall back — the vertex of the arc is 9 feet.

steps: h = 9 − (t − 2)² says: start at the peak height 9, then subtract a penalty for being away from t = 2.
Zero penalty at t = 2, so the highest point of the ball's flight is 9 feet.
